hadith:
Virtues of Prayer at Masjid Makkah and Madinah - Narrated Nafi`:

Ibn `Umar never offered the Duha prayer except on two occasions: (1) Whenever he reached Mecca; and he always used to reach Mecca in the forenoon. He would perform Tawaf round the Ka`ba and then offer two rak`at at the rear of Maqam Ibrahim. (2) Whenever he visited Quba, for he used to visit it every Saturday. When he entered the Mosque, he disliked to leave it without offering a prayer. Ibn `Umar narrated that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to visit the Mosque of Quba (sometime) walking and (sometime) riding. And he (i.e. Ibn `Umar) used to say, "I do only what my companions used to do and I don't forbid anybody to pray at any time during the day or night except that one should not intend to pray at sunrise or sunset."
message: Reflect on the essence of sincerity and dependence on Allah, as highlighted in Surah Al-Ikhlas. Emulate the Prophet Muhammad's practice of visiting sacred mosques like those in Mecca and Medina, where prayers hold special virtue. Remember that Allah is Al-Haqq, the ultimate source of truth and justice, guiding us towards righteousness.
name:
Al Haqq - الْحَقُّ - The Truth

The name Al Haqq highlights Allah's role as the source of all true knowledge and the ultimate arbiter of justice. It emphasizes that all matters will return to Him and that He is the foundation upon which truth and justice are built.
verse:
Al-Ikhlas - The Sincerity - 112:2

Allah—the Sustainer ˹needed by all˺.
